description:
FILED s521 (Fable, 2026-10-18 21:0x) from the FULL companion `--all --jobs 4 --bless-stamps` on MAIN-READY-36 (review/companion-full-s521.log): comp/require.t 911/836 -> 908/839 against its snapshot (last measured s507, 2026-10-04 -- the file is QUICK-CAPPED at 450 s and runs only in the full form): 3 NEW rows + 3 FIXED rows.  A one-file run on the 5e6e241d extraction (MAIN-READY-30, before today's six merges; review/require-base30.log) reads the SAME 908/839 with the same rows -- so the move lies in the s507..s520 WINDOW, not in s521's merges; it is not attributed to a merge (a bisect over the 2026-10-05..17 MAIN-READYs would need extractions of those shas and a 450 s run each; do it if the cause below does not explain it outright).

THE ROWS (t/comp/require.t:196-200): bleah.pm is written as
    print "not " if !defined wantarray || wantarray ne '';
    print "ok $i - require() context\n";
    1;
and required four ways (rows 38-41).  perl FORCES SCALAR CONTEXT for `require`, so `wantarray` at the required file's top level is '' (defined, false).  PCL prints "not ok" for all four (row 38 was already blessed under #1688; rows 39-41 passed at s507 and fail since -- the window also FIXED three #1688 rows: test 0 and 1097 `(AA) ... $^P = 10; require / use mttest...` and 1096 `(AB) list return value is simple true value <1>`, so the same change moved both ways: the require-return work of #1688 / module_true (s513-s518) is the natural suspect).

PROBE (write it first): `open my $f, '>', '/tmp/w.pm'; print $f 'print defined wantarray ? (wantarray ? "list" : "scalar") : "void", "\n"; 1;'; require '/tmp/w.pm'; my $x = require '/tmp/w.pm' ...` -- perl prints `scalar` for a plain `require FILE;` statement (and for `my @a = require ...`: scalar too -- the context is FORCED, not inherited); also `do FILE` (perl: do inherits the CALLER's context) and `use`.  PCL's answer per spelling.  FIX SHAPE: the require path (`p-require` / `%p-load-text-stream` / the module loader) binds `*wantarray*` to the scalar value around the file's top-level forms, as perl's pp_require does; `do FILE` keeps the caller's.  ACCEPTANCE: the probe = perl; `tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1 --timeout 450 comp/require.t` back to 911/836 or better (rows 38-41 pass; the three FIXED rows stay fixed); the rows in perl-suite-fails.tsv edited; a guard row in the Pl/t file holding require rows (grep `wantarray` Pl/t); the sweep (cl/).


CORRECTION (Fable, same hour): the blessed file ALREADY held all four `require() context` rows, numbered 38 42 43 44 (perl's numbering at s507); the run numbers them 38-41, so the ROW DIFF's "3 NEW" was a RENUMBERING, not three new failures.  The snapshot still moved 911/836 -> 908/839 (3 rows newly failing, 3 FIXED), and the three newly failing rows cannot be identified from the row files (the s507 raw run is gone).  To settle: one-file runs (`--timeout 450`) on extractions between the s507 stamp (2026-10-04) and MAIN-READY-30, comparing the raw .fails.tsv row lists.  The four rows re-blessed as 38-41 under this task.

=== s528 (Fable, 2026-10-25): the round-5 FULL companion reads 7 of the 8 `require() context` spellings failing (s521 blessed 4) ===
Reduced probe (scratchpad preq/p.pl: bleah.pm prints wantarray at its top level; the 8 spellings of t/comp/require.t:205-213), perl: all 8 `''`.  PCL on main (code 31cd8c02) and on every tree probed back to MAIN-READY-38 (c7135f6f): `$foo = eval q{require bleah}` -> `''` (passes), `@foo = eval q{...}` -> `'1'` (the caller's LIST context leaks into the required file), the six void / block-eval / return spellings -> undef (the caller's VOID context leaks).  So the required file's top level runs under the CALLER's dynamic *wantarray* instead of perl's forced scalar.  FIX SHAPE (ruled): ONE place -- `p-use` (which `p-require` / `p-require-file` / `use` all reach) binds `*wantarray*` to NIL (scalar) around the module body's execution, for BOTH load paths (the text run and the fasl load); nothing at the spellings.  Guard: the 8 spellings in a Pl/t file (perl-probed text), inverse-verified on a main extraction.  Bar: `cl/` change -> the full sweep + a bounded companion leg on comp/require.t (one-file, 450 s allowance) + everyday; the 7 blessed rows (38-44) leave perl-suite-fails.tsv by edit when it lands.  Attribution of 4 -> 7 (s521 -> s528): the real file at the s521 base is being re-run (s528 bisect, `~/pcl-agent-scratch/s528/require-onefile.log`); the reduced probe reads 7 on every tree, so the s521 count may have been the real file's own state (its `$::i` numbering / the by-description pairing of a repeated description -- the s521 snapshot note already says the row identity is not recoverable from the logs).

SETTLED s528 20:2x: NOT a mover -- the REAL file one-file at the s521 base fb1c369f reads 7 failing (rows 38-44), identical to main; the s521 bless had carried 4.  Rows 42-44 added to baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv under this task.  The fix shape above stands; its landing removes all 7 rows by edit.


=== DONE (s529a) ===
Fixed in s529a (2026-10-31, Opus), commit "s529a #3524".  p-load-module-cached binds *wantarray* and *pcl-caller-wantarray* to nil around the module body (fasl load and text run alike).  DEVIATION from the ruled shape, with its reason: the ruling named p-use, but p-require-file's non-.pm arm (`require "x.pl"`) never reaches p-use -- p-load-module-cached is the one loader both require entries reach.  do FILE (p-do) keeps the caller's context, probed (list / scalar / void).  Probe scratch/s529a/pr/w1.pl (15 lines) = perl.  Guard Pl/t/use-require-01.t row 81 (fails on 77c7d9d7).  ir-spec §4.  Companion one-file comp/require.t (--timeout 450): 908/839 -> 915/832; rows 38-44 out of perl-suite-fails.tsv by edit; the ROW DIFF's 7 "NEW" (rows 1096-1102, the #1688 module_true family) were failing before but past the 500-row log cap -- added by edit with that cause; snapshot row in perl-suite-run.tsv edited.

RULING (Fable, s530, on s529a's MERGE-READY): the bind in p-load-module-cached instead of the ruled p-use is ACCEPTED, for the reason above -- p-require-file's non-.pm arm (`require "x.pl"`) never reaches p-use, and p-load-module-cached is the one loader both require entries reach (fasl load and text run alike).
subject: `wantarray` at the TOP LEVEL of a required file is '' in perl (scalar context is FORCED for require); PCL answers something else -- t/comp/require.t rows 38-41 "require() context"; the same window FIXED three #1688 rows
